question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Oblegation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Oblegation" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Obligation", meaning a duty or commitment that one is bound to fulfil. (दायित्व / कर्तव्य)

◦ Example: It is our obligation to help the needy.

• Spelling key: OB + LI + GA + TION (the second syllable is "li", not "le").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Overview", "Opponent" and "Ointment" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related forms: oblige (verb), obligatory (adjective), obligation (noun). Watch the "i" in obligation, not "e".

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

Applicants who are younger and prettier than you will continue appliying.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. appliying.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Appliying" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "applying". When a verb ends in a consonant + "y", the "y" is retained before "-ing" (apply → applying), not changed to "iy". (आवेदन करना)

◦ Example: She is applying for a new job.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "younger", "applicants" and "prettier" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Spelling rule: verbs ending in "-y" keep the "y" before "-ing" (study → studying, apply → applying), but change "y" to "i" before "-ed"/"-er" (apply → applied, pretty → prettier).

question:
Select the option that corrects the error in the given sentence.

She performed bad in the exam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. badly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word modifying the verb "performed" must be an adverb, not an adjective. The adverb form of "bad" is "badly".

◦ Correct: She performed badly in the exam.

• "Bad" is an adjective (describes nouns); "badly" is an adverb (describes verbs).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "good" and Option 3 "goodly" are the wrong meaning (and "good" is also an adjective).

NOTE

• Adjective vs adverb: "She is a bad singer" (adjective + noun) vs "She sings badly" (adverb + verb). Most adverbs of manner end in "-ly".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The late secretary of our society was known for his ruthless treatment of all the security personnel of the society.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Compassionate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ruthless" means having no pity or compassion; cruel and merciless. (निर्दयी / क्रूर)

• Its antonym is "compassionate", meaning kind, sympathetic and merciful.

◦ Example: The compassionate doctor treated the poor free of charge.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Startled" (surprised) and Option 2 "Fragile" (easily broken) are unrelated.

• Option 4 "Brutal" is a synonym of ruthless, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ruthless: merciless, cruel, brutal, heartless. Antonyms: compassionate, merciful, kind, humane.

question:
Select the most appropriate word opposite in meaning (ANTONYM) to the underlined word in the given sentence.

Aunty Hema gave us her candid opinion on the skit we performed on Children's Day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. prejudiced.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Candid" means honest, straightforward and frank; free from bias. (निष्कपट / स्पष्टवादी)

• Its antonym is "prejudiced", meaning biased or holding preconceived opinions.

◦ Example: A judge must not be prejudiced against either party.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "frank" is a synonym of candid.

• Options 1 "strong" and 4 "intelligent" are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of candid: frank, honest, forthright, blunt, open. Antonyms: prejudiced, biased, guarded, evasive.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

An eucalyptus tree in my backyard acts as a landmark for many to reach my house.
option_3: acts as a landmark for many
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. An eucalyptus tree.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound, not the letter. "Eucalyptus" begins with a consonant (/yu/) sound, so it takes "a", not "an".

◦ Correct: A eucalyptus tree in my backyard acts as a landmark ...

• Words like university, union, European and one also begin with a /yu/ or /w/ sound and take "a".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "in my backyard", "acts as a landmark for many" and "to reach my house" are all correct.

NOTE

• Use "an" before a vowel sound (an hour, an MP) and "a" before a consonant sound (a university, a one-rupee coin, a eucalyptus).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The fresh air / in the garden relaxes / the minds of children as / the environment is cleaner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the environment is cleaner.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparative adjective "cleaner" requires a "than" comparison. Here no comparison is intended, so the positive degree "clean" should be used.

◦ Correct: ... the minds of children as the environment is clean.

• Using "cleaner" without "than" is grammatically incomplete.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "The fresh air", "in the garden relaxes" and "the minds of children as" are all correct ("as" here means "because").

NOTE

• Use the comparative only with an explicit or implied "than" (cleaner than X). Without comparison, use the positive degree (clean).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Fetid
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Fragrant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fetid" means having a foul or unpleasant smell; stinking. (दुर्गंधयुक्त)

• Its antonym is "fragrant", meaning having a pleasant, sweet smell.

◦ Example: The garden was full of fragrant roses.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Fatigued" (very tired), Option 3 "False" (untrue) and Option 4 "Fatal" (causing death) are unrelated to smell.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fetid: foul, stinking, putrid, rank, malodorous. Antonyms: fragrant, aromatic, sweet-smelling, perfumed.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

I have a vague memory of meeting her many years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Hazy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vague" means not clear or definite; indistinct. Its closest synonym is "hazy", meaning unclear or blurred. (अस्पष्ट / धुंधला)

◦ Example: I have only a hazy idea of what happened.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "evident" (obvious) and Option 2 "pellucid" (very clear) are antonyms of vague.

• Option 4 "Symbolic" (representing something) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of vague: hazy, unclear, indistinct, blurred, obscure. Antonyms: clear, definite, precise, distinct.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher asked us to _______ our essays for spelling and grammar errors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. revise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Revise" means to re-examine and correct or improve a piece of writing. Checking essays for spelling and grammar errors is exactly this. (संशोधित करना)

◦ Example: Always revise your answers before submitting the paper.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "advise" (to give advice) does not fit the context of correcting essays.

• Option 3 "recognise" (to identify) and Option 4 "revolve" (to turn around) are irrelevant.

NOTE

• Note the noun/verb pair: advise (verb) vs advice (noun). Revise → revision (noun).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The act of talking to oneself, often audibly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Soliloquy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "soliloquy" is the act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone (or regardless of hearers) — i.e. talking to oneself. (आत्मालाप / स्वगत कथन)

◦ Example: Hamlet's "To be or not to be" is a famous soliloquy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Monologue" — a long speech by one person to an audience (not necessarily to oneself).

• Option 2 "Dialogue" — a conversation between two or more people.

• Option 4 "Solitude" — the state of being alone (not speech).

NOTE

• In drama, a soliloquy reveals a character's inner thoughts to the audience while other characters cannot hear.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Show
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cover.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Show" means to display or make something visible. Its antonym is "cover", meaning to hide or conceal. (ढकना / छिपाना)

◦ Example: She covered the painting with a cloth so no one could see it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "Exhibit" and 4 "Display" are synonyms of show.

• Option 3 "Register" (to record) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of show: display, exhibit, reveal, present. Antonyms: cover, hide, conceal, mask.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He hardness ever / complains about / his workload because / he enjoys his job.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He hardness ever.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hardness" is a noun and is wrong here; the intended word is the adverb "hardly". "Hardly ever" means "almost never".

◦ Correct: He hardly ever complains about his workload because he enjoys his job.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "complains about", "his workload because" and "he enjoys his job" are all correct.

NOTE

• "Hardly ever", "rarely" and "seldom" are adverbs of frequency meaning "almost never". Do not confuse "hardly" (adverb) with "hardness" (noun).

question: Your sibling accidentally broke your favourite vase. Which of the following idioms might you use to tell them not to worry about it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. "Don't cry over spilt milk!"

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Don't cry over spilt milk" means there is no use worrying or being upset about something that has already happened and cannot be changed. (बीती बातों पर पछताना बेकार है)

◦ Example: The money is lost, so don't cry over spilt milk — just move on.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Shallow brooks are noisy" — those who know little talk the most.

• Option 3 "Bite the bullet" — to face a difficult situation bravely.

• Option 4 "Walking on air" — feeling extremely happy.

NOTE

• Since the vase is already broken (an unchangeable past event), the idiom about not regretting past mishaps is the right choice.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I dream of a country where even the least talented person has the _______ to earn a living.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. opportunity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Opportunity" means a favourable chance or occasion to do something. The sentence conveys the wish that everyone should get a chance to earn a living. (अवसर)

◦ Example: Education gives poor children the opportunity to improve their lives.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "landmark" (a prominent object/event) and Option 3 "priority" (something more important) do not fit.

• Option 4 "admit" is a verb and grammatically wrong after "the".

NOTE

• Collocations with opportunity: get/have/seize/miss an opportunity, a golden opportunity, equal opportunity.

question:
Select the option that will correct the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no correction is required, select No correction needed.

Naveen is as tall as Rocky.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No correction needed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "as + positive adjective + as" is the correct way to show equality between two people. "Naveen is as tall as Rocky" is grammatically correct, so no change is required.

◦ Example: She is as clever as her sister.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the tallest" (superlative) and Option 2 "taller than" (comparative) would change the meaning and are unnecessary.

• Option 3 "tall as" is incomplete (missing the first "as").

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: positive — "as tall as"; comparative — "taller than"; superlative — "the tallest". Use "as ... as" to show two things are equal.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

How can someone / walk this farthest / just for / peace of mind?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. walk this farthest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the demonstrative "this" (used as an intensifier meaning "to this extent"), we need the positive degree "far", not the superlative "farthest".

◦ Correct: How can someone walk this far just for peace of mind?

• "This far / this much / this long" are fixed adverbial phrases.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "How can someone", "just for" and "peace of mind" are all correct.

NOTE

• Degrees of "far": far – farther/further – farthest/furthest. "This far" (= to this extent) uses the positive degree, not the superlative.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The humble surroundings of our company _______ creativity amongst the newly recruited employees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. inspired.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inspired" means stimulated or encouraged (someone) to do or feel something creative. The surroundings encouraging creativity among employees fits this sense. (प्रेरित किया)

◦ Example: The beautiful landscape inspired the poet to write.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "banished" (drove away) is the opposite sense.

• Option 2 "connected" and Option 3 "filed" do not collocate meaningfully with "creativity".

NOTE

• Synonyms of inspire: motivate, encourage, stimulate, spur, galvanise.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

We agree that Professor Revanth is very knowledgeable, but we do not like attending his classes because he always keeps blowing the trumpet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. blowing his own trumpet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct idiom is "to blow one's own trumpet", meaning to boast or praise oneself. It fits the context of a knowledgeable professor whom students dislike for his self-praise. (अपनी प्रशंसा स्वयं करना)

◦ Example: A truly great person never blows his own trumpet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 change the phrase into literal expressions about a musical trumpet, losing the idiomatic sense of self-praise.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of boasting: to sing one's own praises, to pat oneself on the back. Opposite: to be modest/humble.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

A) Exaggerate  B) Accommodate  C) Exuberant  D) Perservere
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. D (Perservere).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Word D "Perservere" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Persevere", meaning to continue steadfastly despite difficulties. (धैर्यपूर्वक लगे रहना)

◦ Example: If you persevere, you will surely succeed.

• Spelling key: PER + SE + VERE (no extra "r" — it is "perse-", not "perser-").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Exaggerate", "Accommodate" and "Exuberant" are all correctly spelt (note the double letters — exaggerate has "gg", accommodate has "cc" and "mm").

NOTE

• Related forms: persevere (verb), perseverance (noun). Commonly confused spellings: accommodate, exaggerate, perseverance, occurrence.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students want (1)_______ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)_______ valuable to a student's degree. Indian students are highly (3)_______ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)_______ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)_______ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. employability.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a noun (the object of "want") — "Students want employability as the primary outcome of higher education." "Employability" is the noun meaning the quality of being suitable for paid work. (रोज़गार-योग्यता)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "employable" is an adjective, not a noun.

• Options 3 "appointed" (past participle) and 4 "appoint" (verb) do not fit the noun slot after "want".

NOTE

• Word forms: employ (verb), employee/employer/employment/employability (nouns), employable (adjective).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students want (1)_______ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)_______ valuable to a student's degree. Indian students are highly (3)_______ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)_______ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)_______ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. equally.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb "equally" fits best — "practical experience becomes equally valuable to a student's degree", i.e. just as valuable as theoretical learning. (समान रूप से)

◦ Example: Both diet and exercise are equally important for health.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "voicelessly" (without voice) and Option 4 "abruptly" (suddenly) do not fit.

• Option 2 "hardly" (almost not) contradicts the intended positive sense of value.

NOTE

• "Equally" modifies the adjective "valuable"; adverbs of degree (equally, highly, extremely) come before the adjective they modify.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students want (1)_______ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)_______ valuable to a student's degree. Indian students are highly (3)_______ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)_______ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)_______ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. competitive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Competitive" fits the sense — "Indian students are highly competitive at theoretical learning but lack practical training", i.e. strong and eager to outdo others in theory. (प्रतिस्पर्धी)

◦ Example: The exam has become extremely competitive over the years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "spirit" is a noun and does not fit "highly ___ at".

• Option 3 "spiritual" (relating to the spirit) and Option 4 "relaxed" (calm) do not suit the contrast with "lack practical training".

NOTE

• "Highly + adjective" is a common intensifier: highly competitive, highly skilled, highly motivated.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students want (1)_______ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)_______ valuable to a student's degree. Indian students are highly (3)_______ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)_______ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)_______ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. has been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "This" (referring to the single situation) is singular, and the phrase "for decades" signals the present perfect tense. Hence "This has been an issue for decades." (दशकों से एक समस्या रही है)

◦ Example: This has been a problem for years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "have been" is plural and does not agree with the singular "This".

• Option 1 "will be" (future) and Option 4 "is" (simple present) do not convey the "for decades" duration up to now.

NOTE

• Present perfect (has/have been) with "for + period" shows an action or state continuing from the past up to the present.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students want (1)_______ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)_______ valuable to a student's degree. Indian students are highly (3)_______ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)_______ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)_______ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. perennial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Perennial" means lasting or existing for a long time; recurring again and again. It matches the earlier phrase "an issue for decades" and "long-lasting gap". (चिरस्थायी / बारहमासी)

◦ Example: Unemployment is a perennial problem in many countries.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "insignificant" (unimportant) and Option 4 "momentary" (very brief) contradict the "for decades / long-lasting" idea.

• Option 3 "appetite" is a noun and grammatically wrong before "issue".

NOTE

• Synonyms of perennial: enduring, lasting, persistent, recurring, chronic. Antonyms: temporary, momentary, fleeting.

question: In which state is the Kaiga Nuclear Power Project located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kaiga Nuclear Power Project (Kaiga Generating Station) is located in the Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka, on the banks of the Kali river. (कैगा परमाणु ऊर्जा परियोजना — कर्नाटक)

• It is operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) and uses PHWR (Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor) technology.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Some major nuclear power stations in India: Tarapur (Maharashtra), Rawatbhata (Rajasthan), Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu), Kakrapar (Gujarat), Narora (UP), Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu).

NOTE

• India's nuclear programme is overseen by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) and NPCIL; Homi J. Bhabha is called the father of India's nuclear programme.

question: Which element is known for having the highest electronegativity on the periodic table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fluorine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fluorine (F)" has the highest electronegativity of all elements, with a value of about 4.0 on the Pauling scale. (फ्लोरीन — उच्चतम विद्युत ऋणात्मकता)

• Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract shared electrons in a chemical bond.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Electronegativity increases across a period (left to right) and decreases down a group.

• The order of the most electronegative elements is roughly F > O > N ≈ Cl.

NOTE

• Fluorine is the most reactive and most electronegative non-metal; caesium/francium are among the least electronegative (most electropositive) elements.

question: As per the Census 1951, the female literacy rate in India was:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.86%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of 1951 (the first census after independence), the female literacy rate in India was about 8.86%, while the overall literacy rate was around 18.33%. (1951 की जनगणना — महिला साक्षरता 8.86%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Female literacy has risen sharply over the decades, reaching about 64.6% as per Census 2011 (overall literacy ~74%).

• Kerala consistently records the highest female literacy among Indian states.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years; the first census was in 1872 (under Lord Mayo) and the first complete one in 1881 (under Lord Ripon).

question: Theravada is known as the official religion of which of the following neighbouring countries of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sri Lanka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Theravada Buddhism" is the state/official religion associated with Sri Lanka, where it has been the dominant faith for over two thousand years. (थेरवाद बौद्ध धर्म — श्रीलंका)

• Theravada, meaning "Doctrine of the Elders", is the oldest surviving school of Buddhism and uses the Pali Canon (Tipitaka).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Theravada is also the major form of Buddhism in Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia and Laos.

• The other major branch, Mahayana, is prevalent in China, Japan, Korea and Vietnam.

NOTE

• Buddhism was introduced to Sri Lanka by Mahinda and Sanghamitta, children of Emperor Ashoka.

question: Which virus is responsible for causing common cold?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rhinovirus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Rhinovirus" is the most common cause of the common cold (a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract). (सामान्य ज़ुकाम — राइनोवायरस)

• The name comes from Greek "rhino" (nose), as it mainly affects the nose and throat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Hepatitis A virus causes liver infection; the Influenza virus causes flu; certain coronaviruses cause respiratory illnesses (including some colds and COVID-19).

• The common cold is spread by droplets and by touching contaminated surfaces.

NOTE

• There is no cure for the common cold; it is treated symptomatically, and antibiotics do not work against viruses.

question: Which of the following dance awards is organised by the National Institute of Indian Classical Dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abhinandan Saroja.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Abhinandan Saroja" National Dance Award is organised by the National Institute of Indian Classical Dance (NIICD) to honour distinguished contributions to Indian classical dance. (अभिनंदन सरोज राष्ट्रीय नृत्य पुरस्कार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India has eight recognised classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi is the national body that also confers awards for dance, drama and music.

NOTE

• Such institutional awards promote and preserve India's rich classical performing-arts traditions.

question: How many central banks can a country have?
solution_text:
The correct answer is One.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A country generally has only one central bank, which is the apex monetary authority responsible for issuing currency, controlling monetary policy and regulating the banking system. (एक देश में एक ही केंद्रीय बैंक)

• In India, the central bank is the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), established in 1935.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Functions of a central bank: issue of currency, banker to the government, banker's bank, custodian of foreign exchange reserves, lender of last resort and controller of credit.

• The RBI was nationalised in 1949; its first Governor was Sir Osborne Smith, and the first Indian Governor was C. D. Deshmukh.

NOTE

• Examples of other central banks: Federal Reserve (USA), Bank of England (UK), European Central Bank (Eurozone).

question: What is the rate of movement of tectonic plate boundaries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-2 inch per year.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The tectonic plates of the Earth's lithosphere move very slowly, at a rate of about 1–2 inches (a few centimetres) per year — roughly the speed at which human fingernails grow. (विवर्तनिक प्लेटों की गति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Plate movement is driven by convection currents in the mantle.

• Plate boundaries are of three types: convergent (colliding), divergent (moving apart) and transform (sliding past each other).

NOTE

• This slow movement, over millions of years, causes continental drift, earthquakes, volcanoes and the formation of mountains (e.g., the Himalayas from the Indian and Eurasian plates).

question: Which Rigvedic God is considered an intermediary between God and men?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Rigveda, "Agni" (the fire god) is regarded as the intermediary between the gods and human beings, carrying the offerings of the sacrifice (yajna) to the gods. (अग्नि — देवताओं और मनुष्यों के बीच मध्यस्थ)

• Agni holds the second most important position in the Rigveda, with about 200 hymns dedicated to him (after Indra).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Indra — god of rain, thunder and war (most hymns).

• Varuna — upholder of the cosmic and moral order (Rita).

• Yama — god of death.

NOTE

• The Rig Vedic Aryans practised yajnas (fire sacrifices), in which Agni played the central role as the divine messenger.

question: The Uttarakhand Public Services (Horizontal Reservation for Women) Bill, 2022 provides how much reservation to women?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Uttarakhand Public Services (Horizontal Reservation for Women) Bill, 2022 provides 30% horizontal reservation for women (domiciled in Uttarakhand) in state government jobs. (उत्तराखंड — महिलाओं को 30% क्षैतिज आरक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Horizontal reservation cuts across the vertical reservation (SC/ST/OBC categories) — beneficiaries are adjusted within their own vertical category.

• The Bill gave statutory backing to a long-standing policy that had faced legal challenges.

NOTE

• Vertical reservation applies to SC, ST and OBC categories; horizontal reservation applies to groups such as women, persons with disabilities and ex-servicemen.

question: After the decisive battle of Plassey of 1757, who among the following was declared as the Nawab of Bengal by the British?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mir Jafar Ali Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the Battle of Plassey (1757), in which Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah, the British installed Mir Jafar Ali Khan as the Nawab of Bengal as a reward for his betrayal (he had conspired with the British). (प्लासी का युद्ध — मीर जाफर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 and marked the beginning of British political dominance in India.

• Mir Jafar was later replaced by Mir Qasim, whose conflict with the British led to the Battle of Buxar (1764).

NOTE

• Mir Jafar is often remembered as a symbol of treachery in Indian history for aiding the British against his own Nawab.

question: Which of the following is written by Mulk Raj Anand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Untouchable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Untouchable" (1935) is a famous novel written by Mulk Raj Anand. It portrays a single day in the life of Bakha, a young sweeper, exposing the evils of the caste system and untouchability. (मुल्क राज आनंद — 'अनटचेबल')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other works by Mulk Raj Anand: Coolie, Two Leaves and a Bud, The Village and Across the Black Waters.

• The Guide — R. K. Narayan; The Blue Umbrella — Ruskin Bond; The White Tiger — Aravind Adiga.

NOTE

• Mulk Raj Anand, along with R. K. Narayan and Raja Rao, is regarded as a pioneer of Indian English fiction.

question: Ranjani Hebbar was associated with which of the following fields?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carnatic music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ranjani Hebbar was associated with the field of Carnatic music (the classical music tradition of South India). (कर्नाटक संगीत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Carnatic music is the classical music system of southern India, with foundational contributions from the Trinity of Carnatic music — Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

• Hindustani music is the classical tradition of northern India.

NOTE

• Key elements common to both systems: raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic cycle).

question: At which of the following places is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sasaram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is situated at Sasaram in Bihar. It is a magnificent example of Indo-Islamic (Afghan) architecture, built of red sandstone and standing in the middle of an artificial lake. (शेरशाह सूरी का मकबरा — सासाराम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sher Shah Suri (Farid Khan) founded the Sur Empire after defeating Humayun (Battle of Chausa 1539, Kannauj 1540).

• His reforms: introduction of the silver Rupiya coin, the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam), an efficient revenue and postal system.

NOTE

• The tomb is often compared to the Taj Mahal in grandeur and is considered a masterpiece of the Suri period.

question: Akbar's first expedition towards Deccan was sent to Ahmednagar under the leadership of Prince Murad and __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Akbar's first expedition to the Deccan, directed against Ahmednagar, was led by his son Prince Murad along with Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan (a famous noble and poet). (अब्दुल रहीम खान-ए-खाना)

• Ahmednagar was heroically defended by Chand Bibi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan ("Rahim") was one of the Navaratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court and is famous for his Hindi/Braj couplets (dohas).

• Other Navaratnas: Birbal, Todar Mal, Tansen, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Man Singh, etc.

NOTE

• Akbar's Deccan campaigns aimed to extend Mughal authority southward; this policy was continued by later Mughals.

question: Which of the following Biosphere reserves is located in Uttarakhand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nanda Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is located in Uttarakhand, in the Himalayan region around the Nanda Devi peak. It is a UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves site. (नंदा देवी बायोस्फीयर रिज़र्व — उत्तराखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Panchmarhi — Madhya Pradesh; Nilgiri — Tamil Nadu/Kerala/Karnataka (India's first biosphere reserve, 1986); Dihang-Dibang — Arunachal Pradesh.

• The Valley of Flowers and Nanda Devi National Parks together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• A biosphere reserve has three zones — core, buffer and transition — to balance conservation with sustainable development.

question: Padma Subramanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam are distinguished practitioners of __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Padma Subramanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam are all distinguished exponents of Bharatanatyam, the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu. (भरतनाट्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni, and was traditionally performed in temples (Sadir/Dasiattam).

• It is known for fixed upper-body postures, bent knees (araimandi), mudras and expressive abhinaya.

NOTE

• Yamini Krishnamurthy was also renowned for Kuchipudi, but this group is primarily identified with Bharatanatyam.

question: In the year 1930, the Salt Satyagraha was led by who among the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Salt Satyagraha (Dandi March) of 1930 was led by Mahatma Gandhi. He marched from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi (about 240 miles/385 km) and broke the salt law by making salt from seawater on 6 April 1930. (नमक सत्याग्रह — महात्मा गांधी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 and marked the start of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

• It challenged the British salt monopoly/tax and drew worldwide attention to India's freedom struggle.

NOTE

• C. Rajagopalachari led a similar salt march at Vedaranyam in Tamil Nadu; Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana Satyagraha raid on the salt works.

question: Which of the following countries won its 8th Men's Asian Cup cricket title in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won the Asia Cup 2023 (ODI format), which was its 8th Men's Asia Cup cricket title. India beat Sri Lanka in the final, held at the R. Premadasa Stadium, Colombo. (एशिया कप 2023 — भारत का 8वाँ खिताब)

• Mohammed Siraj took 6 wickets in the final, and India bowled Sri Lanka out for just 50 runs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The 2023 Asia Cup was hosted in a hybrid model between Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

• India is the most successful team in the Asia Cup's history.

NOTE

• The Asia Cup alternates between ODI and T20 formats depending on the upcoming ICC world event.

question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in 'Liberty' as per the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Trust and hope.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Preamble guarantees to all citizens "Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship". "Trust and hope" is NOT part of this list. (प्रस्तावना — 'स्वतंत्रता')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Preamble secures four ideals: Justice (social, economic, political), Liberty (of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship), Equality (of status and opportunity) and Fraternity (assuring dignity and unity).

• The words Socialist, Secular and Integrity were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

NOTE

• The Preamble is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru and describes India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.

question: In February 2023, who was appointed as the CEO of NITI Aayog?
solution_text:
The correct answer is BVR Subrahmanyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2023, senior IAS officer BVR Subrahmanyam was appointed the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NITI Aayog, succeeding Parameswaran Iyer. (नीति आयोग के सीईओ — बी.वी.आर. सुब्रह्मण्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is a policy think tank of the Government of India, established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

• Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister; its administrative head is the CEO.

NOTE

• NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up "cooperative federalism" approach, unlike the top-down Planning Commission with its Five-Year Plans.

question: Based on the number of chambers in the heart, select the odd one from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Crocodile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The crocodile is the odd one out because it has a four-chambered heart (two atria and two ventricles), whereas the turtle, chameleon and frog have a three-chambered heart (two atria and one ventricle). (मगरमच्छ — चार-कक्षीय हृदय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Crocodiles are unique among reptiles in having a completely divided (four-chambered) heart, though they have a special connection (foramen of Panizza).

• Amphibians (frog) and most reptiles (turtle, chameleon) have three-chambered hearts; birds and mammals have four-chambered hearts.

NOTE

• Chamber count: Fishes – 2; Amphibians & most Reptiles – 3; Crocodiles, Birds & Mammals – 4.

question: In which of the following years was the 11th Fundamental Duty added in the Indian Constitution through the 86th Amendment Act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2002.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 11th Fundamental Duty was added to the Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. Under Article 51A(k), it is the duty of every parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child (or ward) between the ages of 6 and 14 years. (11वाँ मौलिक कर्तव्य — 2002)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The original 10 Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• The 86th Amendment also inserted Article 21A (Right to Education as a fundamental right).

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IV-A (Article 51A) of the Constitution and are non-justiciable.

question: What does the term 'deuce' signify in tennis?
option_3: The final point in a game
solution_text:
The correct answer is A tied score at 40-40.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In tennis, "deuce" signifies a tied score of 40–40 in a game. From deuce, a player must win two consecutive points (advantage, then game) to win the game. (ड्यूस — 40-40 की बराबरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Tennis scoring within a game: 0 (love), 15, 30, 40, then game. At 40–40 it is deuce; the point after deuce is advantage.

• A "let" is a serve that touches the net but lands in; a "fault" is an invalid serve.

NOTE

• Major tennis tournaments (Grand Slams): Australian Open, French Open (Roland Garros), Wimbledon and US Open.

question: A regal ceremony in the form of Beating Retreat ceremony on the evening of __________ marks the end of Republic Day celebrations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 29th January.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Beating Retreat" ceremony, held on the evening of 29 January every year, formally marks the end of the Republic Day celebrations. (बीटिंग रिट्रीट — 29 जनवरी)

• It is performed at Vijay Chowk in New Delhi by the bands of the three armed forces — the Army, Navy and Air Force.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Republic Day celebrations begin on 24 January and span up to 29 January.

• The ceremony is a centuries-old military tradition marking the recall of troops from the battlefield at dusk.

NOTE

• A popular tune played at the ceremony has traditionally been "Abide With Me"; in recent years the repertoire has featured more Indian compositions.
